title: Marriage and Divorce in Islam and Christianity
subtitle: Consent, mercy, divorce, polygyny, and protection from harm in Islamic marriage
summary: Islam treats marriage as a serious covenant of mercy, financial responsibility, and mutual rights. Authentic hadith support the bride's permission, and contemporary institutions explicitly reject forced marriage. Classical jurists differed over some guardianship powers, but abuse and harm violate duties of protection. Divorce and independent routes to separation give recourse when a marriage cannot be repaired; polygyny is a conditional permission tied to justice.

seo.metaTitle: Marriage and Divorce in Islam and Christianity: Scriptural and Legal Perspectives
seo.metaDescription: Islamic marriage is built on consent, mercy, mutual rights, financial responsibility, regulated divorce, and firm protection from abuse and coercion.

sections.title: A Serious Covenant Needs Both Rights and a Way Out
sections.body:
Quran 30:21 describes marriage through tranquility, affection, and mercy; 4:21 calls it a solemn covenant. The Islamic case is that a family needs commitments, financial duties, consent, and protection when those commitments fail.

It is not a claim that every spouse has identical legal powers. Polygyny, guardianship, and access to divorce raise real objections. Their conditions and disagreements belong in the explanation, not in fine print after an idealized picture.

sections.title: Consent and Financial Security
sections.body:
Authentic hadith support a woman's right to accept or refuse a husband. [Sahih al-Bukhari 5136](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5136) requires consultation of a previously married woman and permission from a virgin. [Bukhari 5138](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5138) reports that the Prophet invalidated a marriage arranged against Khansa bint Khidam's wishes. Egypt's [Dar al-Ifta](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/fatwa/details/8323/a-woman%E2%80%99s-right-to-choose-her-husband) explicitly requires the bride's consent and rejects forced marriage.

[Classical jurists differed](https://journalofislamiclaw.com/current/article/download/scheunchen/117?inline=1) over a father's power to arrange marriage for virgin or minor wards, often called ijbar. The historical rules were therefore not uniform. It is not a license for relatives to coerce a woman or expose her to harm. A shy bride's silence in the hadith follows a request for permission; it must not be used to dismiss refusal or fear.

The mahr belongs to the bride, and marriage does not transfer her property to her husband. The husband provides according to his means, while both spouses owe faithful and honorable treatment. Quran 4:19 commands men to live with their wives in kindness.

sections.title: Permission Without a General First-Wife Veto
sections.body:
Quran 4:3 permits up to four wives and directs a man to one if he fears injustice. Quran 4:129 recognizes the limits of emotional equality and forbids leaving a wife suspended. These conditions are real, but they do not mean the first wife must agree to the arrangement.

Her consent was not a general classical condition for a second marriage. Egypt's [Dar al-Ifta states this explicitly](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/fatwa/details/8199/is-the-consent-of-the-first-wife-to-a-second-marriage-obligatory), while distinguishing present laws that can impose additional requirements. Valid contractual conditions and legal remedies also vary. Justice must not be described as a guarantee that she chose the marriage's changed terms or will not suffer.

The Islamic defense is that an additional recognized family can be lawful without making exclusivity an automatic condition of every marriage. That is a genuine asymmetry, not proof that a wife's preference for exclusivity is selfish. Its defensibility depends on obligations that restrain the husband's power: maintenance, housing, and fair division of time are enforceable rights, not gifts. [Dar al-Ifta's discussion of co-wives' rights](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/fatwa/details/8249/is-it-permissible-to-keep-my-first-wife-who-waived-her-conjugal-rights-and-marry) gives concrete examples.

A husband must obey applicable protective law and valid conditions, and a wife needs workable access to the separation remedies available in her legal system. Those remedies are not an automatic veto or effortless escape. A lawful permission cannot make neglect righteous, and inability to fulfill justice is a reason not to exercise it.

sections.title: Women Have Routes to Separation, but the Routes Differ
sections.body:
Quran 2:231 forbids retaining a wife to harm her and calls for honorable reconciliation or release. A husband's talaq, a wife's negotiated khul, delegated divorce where valid, and judicial dissolution are distinct procedures, not identical powers with different names. School and state rules differ.

[Sahih al-Bukhari 5274](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5274) records the wife of Thabit ibn Qays seeking separation without accusing him of bad character or religion and returning the garden given as her marital gift. It shows that a woman's need for release is not restricted to proving physical violence.

A serious weakness in practice arises when a husband withholds release and courts are inaccessible. Islam's moral defense requires workable remedies and enforcement of rights, not merely the statement that a remedy exists in theory. Specific cases need competent legal and religious advice.

sections.title: A Husband's Authority Does Not Excuse Harm
sections.body:
Aisha reports that the Prophet never struck a woman or servant ([Sahih Muslim 2328a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2328a)). The example of excellence is honorable treatment, not control through fear.

The classical permission for a tightly restricted non-injurious measure and differing present interpretations are examined in [Women in the Quran and Bible](/articles/women-in-the-quran-and-bible). That history does not legalize injury or remove a victim's need for safety. A dangerous marriage requires protection and competent help, not pressure to preserve appearances.

sections.title: Age, Consummation, and Protection Need a Direct Answer
sections.body:
[Sahih al-Bukhari 5134](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5134) reports Aisha's marriage contract at six and consummation at nine. These widely accepted Sunni reports should not be dismissed through convenient but weak arithmetic. Premodern jurists permitted some guardian-contracted marriages before puberty, and some classical rules also permitted consummation before puberty when physical capacity was judged sufficient. There was no universal classical rule requiring puberty first.

[The legal texts collected in this Islamweb ruling](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/fatwa/print.php?id=195133), including al-Nawawi and the Fatawa Hindiyya, explicitly distinguish judged capacity from puberty. Such a judgment was not equivalent to modern adult consent or proof of psychological safety. That difference is part of the moral question, not a detail answered simply by mentioning guardianship.

Egypt's [Dar al-Ifta discussion of marrying a minor](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/fatwa/details/8184/what-is-the-ruling-on-marrying-a-minor) acknowledges classical permissions without a fixed minimum age while supporting protective age regulation. The present Islamic case for protection must address health, maturity, consent, and the ability to shoulder marriage's duties, not merely repeat a past capacity assessment. Historical permission is not a command to reproduce it today. No appeal to precedent justifies exploitation, disregarding harm, or evading applicable protective law.

sections.title: Mercy Must Be Protected by Practice
sections.body:
Islam's positive case combines an honored covenant with financial rights, responsibility, and lawful release. It does not require pretending that its legal powers are symmetrical or that every historical rule matches contemporary expectations.

For a seeker, the question is whether that framework can order family life toward justice under God. For Muslims, the test includes enforcing women's rights when doing so is inconvenient. Continue to [Women in the Quran and Bible](/articles/women-in-the-quran-and-bible) for the wider foundation of dignity and accountability.

quranVerses.arabic: وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا۟ فِى ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ فَٱنكِحُوا۟ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَ ۖ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ فَوَٰحِدَةً أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعُولُوا۟
quranVerses.translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of [other] women, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one or those your right hand possesses. That is more suitable that you may not incline [to injustice].
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنكِحَ زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُۥ ۗ فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ إِن ظَنَّآ أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍۢ يَعْلَمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And if he has divorced her [for the third time], then she is not lawful to him afterward until [after] she marries a husband other than him. And if the latter husband divorces her [or dies], there is no blame upon the woman and her former husband for returning to each other if they think that they can keep [within] the limits of Allah. These are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍۢ ۚ وَلَا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَارًۭا لِّتَعْتَدُوا۟ ۚ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُۥ ۚ وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ هُزُوًۭا ۚ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَٱلْحِكْمَةِ يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: And when you divorce women and they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms, and do not keep them, intending harm, to transgress [against them]. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself. And do not take the verses of Allah in jest. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom by which He instructs you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Knowing of all things.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ أَن يَنكِحْنَ أَزْوَٰجَهُنَّ إِذَا تَرَٰضَوْا۟ بَيْنَهُم بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ مِنكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ ۗ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَزْكَىٰ لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term, do not prevent them from remarrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an acceptable basis. That is instructed to whoever of you believes in Allah and the Last Day. That is better for you and purer, and Allah knows and you know not.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ وَٱلْوَٰلِدَٰتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَٰدَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ ۖ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ ٱلرَّضَاعَةَ ۚ وَعَلَى ٱلْمَوْلُودِ لَهُۥ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَا تُضَآرَّ وَٰلِدَةٌۢ بِوَلَدِهَا وَلَا مَوْلُودٌۭ لَّهُۥ بِوَلَدِهِۦ ۚ وَعَلَى ٱلْوَارِثِ مِثْلُ ذَٰلِكَ ۗ فَإِنْ أَرَادَا فِصَالًا عَن تَرَاضٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍۢ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا ۗ وَإِنْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن تَسْتَرْضِعُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا سَلَّمْتُم مَّآ ءَاتَيْتُم بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۗ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: Mothers may breastfeed their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing [period]. Upon the father is the mothers' provision and their clothing according to what is acceptable. No person is charged with more than his capacity. No mother should be harmed through her child, and no father through his child. And upon the [father's] heir is [a duty] like that [of the father]. And if they both desire weaning through mutual consent from both of them and consultation, there is no blame upon either of them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by a substitute, there is no blame upon you as long as you give payment according to what is acceptable. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Seeing of what you do.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَٰجًۭا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍۢ وَعَشْرًۭا ۖ فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - they, [the wives, shall] wait four months and ten [days]. And when they have fulfilled their term, then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And Allah is [fully] Acquainted with what you do.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِۦ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّآ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًۭا مَّعْرُوفًۭا ۚ وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا۟ عُقْدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ ۚ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ فَٱحْذَرُوهُ ۚ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: There is no blame upon you for that to which you [indirectly] allude concerning a proposal to women or for what you conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will have them in mind. But do not promise them secretly except for saying a proper saying. And do not determine to undertake a marriage contract until the decreed period reaches its end. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: لَّا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِن طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا۟ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةًۭ ۚ وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى ٱلْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُۥ وَعَلَى ٱلْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُۥ مَتَٰعًۢا بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۖ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
quranVerses.translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women you have not touched nor specified for them an obligation. But give them [a gift of] compensation - the wealthy according to his capability and the poor according to his capability - a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the doers of good.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَن تَسْتَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ بَيْنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ ۖ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا۟ كُلَّ ٱلْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوهَا كَٱلْمُعَلَّقَةِ ۚ وَإِن تُصْلِحُوا۟ وَتَتَّقُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًۭا رَّحِيمًۭا
quranVerses.translation: And you will never be able to be equal [in feeling] between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَٱبْتَلُوا۟ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُوا۟ ٱلنِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ ءَانَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًۭا فَٱدْفَعُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَآ إِسْرَافًۭا وَبِدَارًا أَن يَكْبَرُوا۟ ۚ وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيًّۭا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرًۭا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبًۭا
quranVerses.translation: And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, release their property to them. And do not consume it excessively and quickly, [anticipating] that they will grow up. And whoever, [when acting as guardian], is self-sufficient should refrain [from taking a fee]; and whoever is poor - let him take according to what is acceptable. Then when you release their property to them, bring witnesses upon them. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا لِّتَسْكُنُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةًۭ وَرَحْمَةً ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُۥ وَقَدْ أَفْضَىٰ بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ وَأَخَذْنَ مِنكُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظًۭا
quranVerses.translation: And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُوا۟ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهًۭا ۖ وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا۟ بِبَعْضِ مَآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٍۢ مُّبَيِّنَةٍۢ ۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ فَإِن كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيْـًۭٔا وَيَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًۭا كَثِيرًۭا
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِ ۖ فَإِمْسَاكٌۢ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌۢ بِإِحْسَٰنٍۢ ۗ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُوا۟ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِۦ ۗ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا ۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep [within] the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep [within] the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah - it is those who are the wrongdoers.

bibleVerses.text: Pharisees came to him, testing him, and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?’ So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”

They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a bill of divorce, and divorce her?” He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so. I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”

His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.” But he said to them, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”

Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman. But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.

Let the husband give his wife the affection owed her, and likewise also the wife her husband. The wife doesn’t have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise also the husband doesn’t have authority over his own body, but the wife. Don’t deprive one another, unless it is by consent for a season, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer, and may be together again, that Satan doesn’t tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

But to the married I command—not I, but the Lord—that the wife not leave her husband (but if she departs, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not leave his wife.

But to the rest I—not the Lord—say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her. The woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is content to live with her, let her not leave her husband. For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy. Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us in peace.

Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy. Therefore I think that because of the distress that is on us, that it’s good for a man to remain as he is. Are you bound to a wife? Don’t seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? Don’t seek a wife. But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.

faq.question: Can a woman be forced to marry?
faq.answer: The cited authentic hadith require a bride's permission and record the rejection of a marriage arranged against a woman's wishes. Contemporary institutions such as Dar al-Ifta explicitly reject forced marriage. Classical jurists differed over certain guardianship powers concerning virgin or minor wards; this history must not be used to justify coercion or harm.

faq.question: Does Islam require polygyny?
faq.answer: No. Quran 4:3 makes it conditional on justice and directs a man to one wife if he fears injustice. A first wife's consent was not a general classical condition for another marriage, though valid contracts and present law may add requirements. Her rights and access to remedies must be protected; permission does not imply that she chose the arrangement or cannot be harmed by it.

faq.question: Can a Muslim woman seek divorce?
faq.answer: Yes, through routes including khul, delegated divorce where applicable, and judicial dissolution. The procedures are not identical to a husband's talaq and vary by school and legal system. Real access matters; a theoretical remedy should not be used to dismiss someone trapped by obstruction or danger.

faq.question: Does Islam permit domestic abuse?
faq.answer: Islamic duties do not authorize injurious domestic abuse, and the Prophet never struck a woman or servant. Many classical jurists nevertheless permitted a restricted non-injurious measure in interpreting the marital-conflict passage. That difficult history should be acknowledged while prioritizing safety, legal protection, and the Prophetic model of honorable treatment.
